newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise after rate cut.

text.p: Israeli shares rose mildly as a rise in Teva Pharmaceutical Industries and Koor Industries prevented the market from falling following a lower than expected interest rate cut, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.66 percent, or 1.29 points, to 197.31 on an all-share turnover of 100 million shekels against 80 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur.
The Maof 25 index gained 0.56 percent to 206.92.
On Tuesday, the Bank of Israel lowered its key lending rate for October by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised nominal rate of 15.5 percent.
"The market expected an interest rate cut of at least 0.5 percentage point. The central bank's decision is a real disappointment," said Izik Winish at Capital Securities.

"If the rate would have been lowered by more than 0.5 percentage point the whole market would have gained 2.0 to 2.5 percent today. Only Teva and Koor prevented the market from falling," Winish added.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share surged 7.5 percent to 143,874 on very high volume of 20 million shekels.

On Thursday a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel voted to back Teva's multiple sclerosis drug Copaxone. The announcement came out late Thursday night and Tuesday was the first time the Israeli market reacted to the news, since Thursday was the last day of trading before the Jewish holiday.

Koor Industries, the second most active share, rose 3.0 percent to 28,925 on turnover of 13 million shekels. Traders said that Koor's shares traded in New York are still traded at a price which is two percent higher than their price in Tel Aviv.
"Half of the activity today was in the leading stocks Teva, Koor and Bezeq Israel Telecom. The activity in these shares prevented the market from falling," said one trader.
"The central bank's decision has stopped the positive momentum. The market has showed strength in the past month but now it is difficult to predict if the positive trend will continue," he said.

Bezeq, the third most active share, lost 0.25 percent to 843 on volume of 9.5 million shekels. Traders said someone was purchasing a large amount of shares in Bezeq for the forth consecutive session. The identity of the buyer was unknown.

The Blue Square Chain Stores Properties & Investments closed unchanged at 2,312 after Bank Hapoalim valued the company at $267 million to $280 million against a market value of $214 million on September 3.
